name: Two Chairs
one_liner: Therapy practice that matches you with a staff therapist after an intake call; video in 15+ states, in person in CA, WA and FL.
best_for: Adults with anxiety or depression who want help finding a therapist who fits
People in California, Washington or Florida who want in-person sessions
People with out-of-network benefits, or Aetna or Kaiser in some areas
People who like tracking progress with regular check-ins
not_for: Anyone in crisis: call or text 988
People who need low-cost therapy without out-of-network benefits
People who need intensive or inpatient care
short_description: Therapist matching and weekly therapy with employed clinicians, by video in 15+ states or in person in CA, WA and FL; mostly out-of-network.
long_description: Two Chairs is a US mental health practice whose therapists are employees rather than contractors. After an initial matching appointment, it assigns you a therapist based on your concerns and preferences, and tracks progress with regular depression and anxiety questionnaires (measurement-based care). Sessions are by video in more than 15 states, or in person at clinics in the San Francisco Bay Area, Los Angeles, Seattle and Miami; psychiatry is offered in about ten states including California, Florida, New York, Texas and Washington. Two Chairs is out-of-network with most insurers (self-pay and out-of-network prices are the same, and out-of-network benefits may cover 60–80%), but in network with some plans such as Aetna and Kaiser in some areas. Third-party sources put self-pay at about $175–$200 or more per session. Two Chairs researchers published a retrospective study of 2,984 of its patients in JMIR Formative Research (2025), finding 71% reliably improved or recovered by session 12; there was no control group.
patient_summary: You start with a matching appointment, then Two Chairs pairs you with one of its employed therapists for weekly sessions by video or at a clinic in the Bay Area, Los Angeles, Seattle or Miami, with symptom check-ins along the way. It is out-of-network with most insurers, so you pay up front and may get part back; it is in network with some plans such as Aetna and Kaiser in some areas. Psychiatry is offered in some states.

pricing.starting_price: Copay with in-network insurance; about $175–$200/session self-pay or out-of-network (third-party estimate)
pricing.notes: Two Chairs is out-of-network with most insurers; self-pay and out-of-network prices are the same, and out-of-network benefits may reimburse 60–80%. In network with some plans (e.g. Aetna, Kaiser in some areas); it says some clients pay $0 and most under $30/session after the deductible. Self-pay figure is from VirtualCareFinder; a competitor (Rula) reports $260 first session and $226 after.

privacy.notes: Website policy (read 2026-10-27, last updated 2022) lists sharing only with therapists, service providers, affiliates and legal or merger recipients and lists no advertising use, but never states whether it sells data; it offers access and updates, not deletion.

seo.title: Two Chairs: W2 Employment for Therapists | HeyPsych
seo.meta_description: Two Chairs provides therapist matching and therapy services with a research-backed matching process, primarily serving California and expanding markets.

faqs.a: Two Chairs primarily serves California, with physical offices in San Francisco, Oakland, Los Angeles, and other Bay Area/LA locations. They offer video therapy throughout California. Check their website for current availability in your area.

faqs.q: How does Two Chairs' matching process work?
faqs.a: You start with a free consultation call to discuss your needs. Two Chairs uses a research-backed process to match you with a therapist based on your concerns, personality, and preferences. The focus on fit reflects research showing the relationship matters for outcomes.
Yes, Two Chairs accepts many major insurance plans in their service areas. They also offer sliding scale for self-pay clients. Contact them to verify your specific insurance coverage.

faqs.q: What makes Two Chairs different from other therapy platforms?
faqs.a: Two Chairs emphasizes matching quality over quick access. Their research-backed process aims to find the right therapist fit, which studies show predicts better outcomes. They also operate physical offices for in-person sessions in addition to video.
